progress.title: Follow your students
steps: Open the class. The Students table updates live — no need to reload.
The green dot means the student saved in the last 2 minutes. "Last save" can lag up to a minute behind their screen (autosave).
Progress shows how many lines of HTML, CSS and JS each student has written. ✨ AI means their last change came from AI help.
View code shows their files and a live preview that refreshes every time they save — great on a projector.
Page → Open ↗ appears once the student has published.

reopenStudent.title: A student comes back (same computer)
steps: The student opens the class link again (or types the class code on the home page).
The editor opens with their saved work. No name needed.
This works even if the class is closed — closing only blocks new students and publishing.

moveWork.title: A student lost their work (other computer, cleared browser, private window)
steps: The student joins again with the same name. They now appear twice in the table.
On the OLD entry click Move work, choose the NEW entry, and confirm.
Their work appears in their editor within a few seconds. Their published link keeps working.

reopenTeacher.title: Your teacher access
steps: On this computer you stay in until you click Exit.
On another computer: open your personal link (🔗 My link shows it, and you can send it to your WhatsApp or email).
Lost it? Ask the bootcamp organizer to send it again.

tips.title: Tips
steps: Ask students to use the same computer and a normal (not private) window every class.
Ask them to press Save before leaving.
Close the class at the end of the bootcamp to freeze publishing.

guide.title: Teacher & mentor guide
guide.lockedIntro: For the bootcamp team. Ask the admin for the password.
guide.intro: Everything you need to run a class. Mentors: start with the first part. Admin: the second part is for you.

enter.title: 1. Enter your dashboard
steps: First time: open the teacher invite link the admin shared in the teachers' group, type your name and press Start.
Right after, press "Send to my WhatsApp" (or email/copy) to keep your personal link. That link is your key: don't share it with students.
Next times on the same computer: open the site and click "I'm a teacher" — you're already in.
On another computer: open your personal link. In the dashboard, 🔗 My link shows it again.

createClass.title: 2. Create a class and let students in
steps: In the dashboard: type the class name, choose the language and the AI tool (Gemini or ChatGPT), press Create class.
Open the class. Project the class code (e.g. K7QM-4TZP) or the QR, or paste the link in the class chat.
Students open the link (or type the code on the home page), write their name and start. Under-13s work in pairs: both names, e.g. "Ana y Luis".

duringClass.title: 3. During the class
steps: The Students table updates live. Green dot = saved in the last 2 minutes. Progress = lines of HTML / CSS / JS.
View code shows a student's files and live preview — great on the projector to review work together.
Everyone has index.html, style.css and script.js. Tailwind (v3) and GSAP are already loaded: no <script> or <link> needed.
✨ AI help: the student writes what they want, copies the prompt to Gemini/ChatGPT, pastes the answer back, reviews the changes and presses Apply.
Errors appear in the Console under the preview, explained in simple words.

studentFaq.title: 4. Common student questions
steps: "I closed the tab": open the class link again on the same computer (or type the class code on the home page). Their work is there.
"I'm on another computer / my work is gone": they join again with the same name; in the dashboard click Move work on the OLD entry and choose the NEW one.
"Where is my page link?": press Publish again (same link), or see Page → Open ↗ in your dashboard.
"My page looks broken": check the Console under the preview; press Reload; make sure tags are closed.
"I lost my changes": remind them to press Save (or Ctrl/Cmd+S); autosave runs every minute.

endOfClass.title: 5. End of class
steps: Ask everyone to press Save and Publish.
Collect the published links from the Page column.
At the end of the bootcamp, switch the class to Closed: no new students and no more publishing; pages stay online.

beforeBootcamp.title: A. Before the bootcamp
steps: Clean old data from a computer with the project: npm run reset:classes (keeps teachers) or npm run reset:all (teachers sign up again). It asks you to type the project name to confirm.
Check the registration code in Firestore: config → registration → code. Change it for each bootcamp if you like.
Share the teacher invite link only in the teachers' group: https://editorweb-29040.web.app/teacher/join/<registration code>.
Do a 5-minute rehearsal: one teacher, two students in private windows, publish a page, try AI help.

duringBootcamp.title: B. During the bootcamp
steps: A teacher lost their personal link: in Firestore open teacherKeys, find their name; the document id is the key. Send them https://editorweb-29040.web.app/t/<document id>.
An inappropriate page: the class teacher presses Unpublish in the dashboard.
"Free daily limit reached": the free plan resets every day; work is safe, try again tomorrow.

afterBootcamp.title: C. After the bootcamp
steps: Close all classes so pages stay online but nothing changes.
Before the next bootcamp, run the reset again (step A).
